stories.headline: Pakistan announces Islamabad meeting of ECO Council of Ministers for 15–16 November
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office announced on 14 November that Islamabad would host the 30th Economic Cooperation Organization Council of Ministers meeting on 15–16 November 2026. The gathering is scheduled, not yet completed; Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar is expected to chair it.
stories.background: ECO is a regional intergovernmental organisation focused on economic connectivity, trade and cooperation. Pakistan holds the ECO chairmanship for 2026–27.
stories.why_it_matters: The ministerial agenda offers a platform for regional connectivity and trade diplomacy, but planned discussions should not be mistaken for adopted agreements.
stories.pakistan_perspective: The announced theme, 'Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO', reflects Pakistan's stated regional-cooperation priorities.
key_takeaways: The 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting was announced for Islamabad on 15–16 November 2026.
quick_gk: Pakistan announced that Islamabad would host the 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting on 15–16 November 2026.
question_angles: Which city was announced on 14 November as host of the 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting?

sources.title: Pakistan to host 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting on Nov 15-16

stories.headline: UN climate chief urges COP31 negotiators to accelerate talks amid fossil-fuel divisions
stories.summary: Reuters reported on 14 November that UN climate chief Simon Stiell urged COP31 negotiators in Antalya, Türkiye, to move quickly on difficult issues and avoid tactical delays. Disagreements over fossil-fuel language and climate finance remained unresolved; no final agreement was reported.
stories.background: COP31 negotiations address implementation of international climate commitments, adaptation finance and the transition away from fossil fuels.
stories.why_it_matters: Disputes over fossil-fuel wording and finance affect the credibility and implementation of international climate cooperation.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Pakistan's climate vulnerability makes adaptation funding and clarity on actual financial commitments especially important.
key_takeaways: Simon Stiell urged faster negotiations at COP31 on 14 November; the final outcome remained pending.
quick_gk: UN climate chief Simon Stiell urged COP31 delegates in Antalya to accelerate negotiations on 14 November 2026.
question_angles: Who urged COP31 negotiators to avoid tactical delays on 14 November 2026?

sources.title: UN climate chief urges speed as COP31 confronts fossil fuel divide

stories.headline: India sets out ambition to reach 900 GW of non-fossil electricity capacity by 2035
stories.summary: Associated Press reported on 14 November that India aims to raise non-fossil electricity capacity to 900 gigawatts by 2035, from a little over 300 GW. Transmission, storage and rising demand remain significant constraints; the target is not capacity already installed.
stories.background: Installed renewable capacity and electricity actually delivered differ because grid congestion, storage limitations and generation profiles affect usable output.
stories.why_it_matters: India's plan illustrates the scale of investment needed to expand low-carbon power while maintaining grid reliability.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Pakistan faces related questions around grid investment, renewable integration, power-sector affordability and energy-import dependence.
key_takeaways: India's reported non-fossil electricity capacity ambition is 900 GW by 2035.
quick_gk: India aims for 900 GW of non-fossil electricity capacity by 2035, according to AP reporting on 14 November 2026.
question_angles: What non-fossil power capacity target for 2035 did India outline in November 2026?

sources.title: India seeks to triple clean energy capacity to 900 gigawatts by 2035, but major hurdles remain

stories.headline: Punjab deploys rapid-response units against crop-residue fires as Lahore battles smog
stories.summary: Reuters reported on 14 November that Punjab had deployed 67 rapid-response units involving 750 officers to respond to crop-residue burning. Officials described enforcement and machinery subsidies, but severe air-pollution exposure remained a concern. Reported enforcement outcomes are official claims, not proof that the wider smog crisis has ended.
stories.what_happened: Punjab's anti-smog teams seek to reach reported agricultural fires within 10–15 minutes; authorities reported extinguishing 650 of 679 fires in one day. The government also subsidises super seeders to reduce the need to burn stubble.
stories.background: Crop burning is one contributor to seasonal particulate pollution, alongside transport, industry, meteorology and cross-border sources.
stories.why_it_matters: The response illustrates the combination of enforcement, agricultural technology and regional cooperation needed to reduce harmful air pollution.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Assess the effectiveness of stubble management without attributing all Lahore smog to a single source; distinguish official statistics from independently measured air-quality outcomes.
key_takeaways: Reuters reported 67 rapid-response units and 750 officers deployed in Punjab against stubble fires.
quick_gk: Punjab's reported anti-stubble-fire response involved 67 units staffed by 750 officers in November 2026.
question_angles: How many rapid-response units did Punjab deploy against crop-residue fires, according to Reuters on 14 November?

sources.title: As smog hangs over Lahore, Pakistan's new pollution squad races to douse stubble fires

stories.headline: Reuters reports Trump considering holding off further Iran attacks absent new provocations
stories.summary: Reuters reported on 14 November, citing three people familiar with discussions, that US President Donald Trump had told advisers he might hold off attacking Iran if no new provocations came from Tehran or Iran-backed Houthis. The report described a conditional position, not a binding ceasefire or settled policy.
stories.what_happened: The report indicated that US decisions remained contingent on regional developments and further provocations.
stories.background: US–Iran tensions and shipping security in the Gulf influence energy markets and regional diplomacy.
stories.why_it_matters: Conditional restraint could reduce near-term escalation risk, but it does not establish a negotiated settlement.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Pakistan has an interest in Gulf stability because of energy imports, expatriate communities and regional diplomacy.
key_takeaways: The reported US position was conditional on the absence of further provocations.
quick_gk: Reuters reported on 14 November that Trump's possible restraint on Iran attacks was conditional on no new provocations.
question_angles: Which Iran-aligned group in Yemen was specifically mentioned in Reuters' 14 November account?

sources.title: Trump tells advisers he may hold off on Iran attacks barring new provocations, sources say

stories.headline: Zelenskyy raises concerns over proposed European security framework and Ukraine's territorial position
stories.summary: Associated Press reported on 14 November that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticised a US-floated European security framework and rejected surrendering Ukrainian-held territory in Donbas or accepting neutrality. He also identified an energy ceasefire, Black Sea access and prisoner exchanges among Ukraine's diplomatic priorities; proposals and tentative exchanges were not completed agreements.
stories.what_happened: Zelenskyy said European countries should be central to European security decisions and expressed concern that proposals could weaken NATO.
stories.background: Ukraine's security guarantees, sovereignty and future relations with NATO remain major unresolved elements of Russia–Ukraine negotiations.
stories.why_it_matters: The debate connects territorial sovereignty, alliance commitments and the terms of any potential negotiated settlement.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Pakistan's foreign-policy analysis should distinguish proposed security frameworks from adopted treaties and consider implications for international law and trade routes.
key_takeaways: Zelenskyy identified reopening the Black Sea among Ukraine's diplomatic priorities.
quick_gk: Ukraine's reported 14 November diplomatic priorities included an energy ceasefire and reopening the Black Sea.
question_angles: Which maritime region did Zelenskyy identify as a priority to reopen in the 14 November report?

sources.title: Zelenskyy says a new European security framework floated by US could benefit Putin
